xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3705: Ctrl-K search: add Conversations to the type list

plan.title: Ctrl-K search: add Conversations to the type list
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: The Ctrl-K palette's scope-chip row only offers a chip for a result type when results of that type are on screen (availableScopes, CommandPalette.tsx:865-873). Conversation hits exist only after a typed server search, so the Conversations chip is invisible until conversation results already exist, and the scope-reset effect (lines 876-878) silently discards the Ctrl-J initialScope='conversations' on open. The scope machinery itself (PaletteScope union, SCOPE_LABEL, groupScope, accent color) already supports 'conversations' — only chip availability is result-derived.
narratives.Proposal: Pin 'conversations' as a persistent scope in availableScopes via a PINNED_SCOPES constant so the chip renders whenever the chip row renders; make the empty-query hint and loading row copy scope-aware for the conversations scope ('Type to search conversations…' / 'Searching conversations…'); keep the existing swallow-to-empty error convention; document the chip row in docs/DESKTOP-APP.md. No server changes and no ordering changes — scope filtering already preserves upstream rank order, so #3703 (newest-first) and #3704 (ordering toggle) compose on top. Full detail in the PRD at .pan/drafts/PAN-3705.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Changing conversation result ordering (owned by #3703)
- Adding an ordering toggle or any preference persistence (owned by #3704)
- Pinning a Memory chip or altering Memory scope behavior
- Any server change, including /api/palette/search parameters
- Restyling the chip row or adding ARIA pressed-state to the pre-existing chips (parity with existing chips is the requirement)

autoDecisions.summary: Pin the Conversations chip unconditionally rather than probing search capability client-side
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for a first-class type-list entry; the server already returns an empty conversations array when semantic search is unavailable, so a probe would add complexity with no behavior gain.

autoDecisions.summary: Make empty/loading copy scope-aware only for the conversations scope
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue AC requires correct empty/loading states when Conversations is selected; claiming to search 'conversations & memory' while scoped to conversations only would be incorrect, and all other scopes keep the existing strings.

autoDecisions.summary: Preserve the swallow-to-EMPTY_SEARCH error convention instead of adding error UI
autoDecisions.rationale: Every result type already renders the standard no-results empty state on search failure; consistency with existing types outranks a one-off error affordance.

autoDecisions.summary: Do not pin the Memory chip
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requests Conversations only; symmetric pinning of Memory is unrequested behavior change.

autoDecisions.summary: Leave result ordering untouched and guard it with an order-preservation test
autoDecisions.rationale: #3703 and #3704 own ordering and the toggle; this issue only needs to not conflict, and the test makes the composition contract explicit.

items.title: Pin the Conversations scope chip in the Ctrl-K palette

expected_outputs: CommandPalette.test.tsx run passes, including the new 'conversations scope chip (PAN-3705)' describe block

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx, add a PINNED_SCOPES constant (['conversations']) near SCOPE_LABEL and add `for (const s of PINNED_SCOPES) present.add(s);` inside the availableScopes memo (lines 865-873), exactly as shown in the PRD's before/after snippet. Do NOT touch the reset effect, the chip renderer, inScope, visibleGroups, result mapping, or the rank sort. Then add a describe('CommandPalette conversations scope chip (PAN-3705)') block to CommandPalette.test.tsx covering the five ACs below, following the file's existing patterns: vi.useFakeTimers with 120ms debounce advance, installStrictFetchMock stubs (empty search payload as at lines 77-79, plus a conversation-hit payload as at lines 152-188), getByRole('button', { name: 'Conversations' }) for the chip (the text also appears as a cmdk group heading — see the disambiguation pattern at lines 206-214), and [role='option'][data-value] queries for rows.

items.title: Given the palette is open with an empty query and zero conversation results, when the scope-chip row renders, then it renders a Conversations chip button (getByRole('button', { name: 'Conversations' })) alongside the other type chips

Given conversation and non-conversation results are present, when the operator activates the Conversations chip by click and (in a second pass) by Enter on the focused chip button, then the result list renders only rows whose data-value carries the conversation (conv-) id prefix
Given the Conversations scope is active, when the operator activates the All chip, then the result list renders every result type again with no scope filter applied

Given the palette renders with initialScope='conversations' and no conversation results, when the open effects settle, then the Conversations scope survives as the active scope (filtered list stays conversations-scoped) instead of resetting to All

Given two conversation hits with rank 1 and rank 2, when the Conversations scope is active, then the list renders them in ascending rank order (scope filtering preserves upstream ordering, the composition contract for #3703/#3704)
Scope-aware empty and loading copy for the Conversations scope

expected_outputs: CommandPalette.test.tsx run passes, including the new empty/loading/error-state tests

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx, make two strings scope-aware exactly as shown in the PRD before/after snippet: the loading row (lines 951-956) renders 'Searching conversations…' when scope === 'conversations' and keeps 'Searching conversations & memory…' otherwise; the empty-query hint (lines 957-962) renders 'Type to search conversations…' when scope === 'conversations' and keeps 'Start typing…' otherwise. The non-empty-query 'No results for "…"' string stays unchanged. Do not add error UI: a failed /api/palette/search continues to fall back to EMPTY_SEARCH (fetchPaletteSearch, lines 288-291). Extend the PAN-3705 describe block in CommandPalette.test.tsx with the three ACs below (in-flight search = fetch promise that never resolves; error = stub returning Response with status 500).

items.title: Given the Conversations scope is active with an empty query, the empty state renders 'Type to search conversations…' instead of 'Start typing…'
Given the Conversations scope is active while a search is in flight, the loading row renders 'Searching conversations…' instead of 'Searching conversations & memory…'

Given /api/palette/search responds with HTTP 500 while the Conversations scope is active, the palette falls back to the standard 'No results for "…"' empty state and preserves the active Conversations chip
Document the scope chips (incl. Conversations) in docs/DESKTOP-APP.md

expected_outputs: grep prints the new scope-chips subsection naming Conversations inside the 'Cmd+K Command Palette' section
grep prints the new Ctrl+J mention inside the same section

narrative.Action: In docs/DESKTOP-APP.md, extend the 'Cmd+K Command Palette' section (lines 103-118) with a short 'Scope chips' subsection: the chip row under the search input filters results by type (All plus Actions, Commands, Workspaces, Issues, Conversations, Memory as available); Conversations is always offered and limits results to conversation search hits; Cmd/Ctrl+J opens the palette already scoped to Conversations. No other doc changes — docs/USAGE.md:709 is a one-line shortcut table entry and stays as-is.

items.title: grep -n 'Conversations' docs/DESKTOP-APP.md produces a hit inside the 'Cmd+K Command Palette' section that names Conversations as an always-available scope chip limiting results to conversation entries
grep -n 'Ctrl+J' docs/DESKTOP-APP.md produces a hit in the same section stating the shortcut opens the palette scoped to Conversations
